headline: High: MemMachine’s MCP/API outputs can feed slim’s shell/filesystem actions, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, so its outputs can be bridged into slim’s interactive CLI or stdin/stdout workflows. slim can execute shell commands and write files, making it plausible that attacker-controlled content from MemMachine is parsed as instructions. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is copied into slim prompts or scripts without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF slim parses MemMachine-produced text as commands or flags, attacker instructions can be executed.
mitigations: Require a strict allowlist for commands and flags before passing MemMachine output to slim.
Insert a manual review step for any text copied from MemMachine into slim.
Disable MCP bridging between the two agents unless provenance tagging is added.
Use a wrapper that strips code fences, shell metacharacters, and YAML/JSON keys before handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware message signing between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while slim handles filesystem artifacts, environment variables, and certificate private keys. slim also has broad network egress and registry credentials, so a shared workspace or handoff could expose sensitive data. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF MemMachine context is written into files that slim reads, sensitive user facts can leak.
IF slim is pointed at directories containing secrets or keys, those contents can be exposed through its outputs or network calls.
mitigations: Keep MemMachine and slim on separate workspaces.
Do not mount directories containing secrets into slim.
Redact environment variables and private keys before any slim run.
Restrict slim network egress to approved registries only.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine can use an MCP server and network egress, while slim can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, read/write the filesystem, and use Docker Engine APIs. Even without shared-state evidence, both can mutate adjacent resources if orchestrated together, creating overlapping write and network authority. Because the profiles do not show locking or shared-state isolation, the conflict is plausible in default pairings.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory tree, file clobbering or inconsistent artifacts can occur.
IF MemMachine issues API-driven actions while slim rewrites files in the same workflow, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize access with a simple lock file or queue.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same container image or project tree.
Review any file writes from slim before MemMachine consumes them.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and resource leases.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine produces conversational outputs and long-term user facts, and slim can act on files and shell commands. If slim treats MemMachine output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into destructive container or filesystem changes. The profiles show no verification gate between them, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF slim consumes MemMachine output without validation, incorrect facts can drive wrong actions.
IF MemMachine-generated instructions are used to modify files or containers, downstream damage can propagate.
mitigations: Require human approval before slim executes any MemMachine-derived action.
Add schema validation for MemMachine outputs before downstream use.
Have slim re-check critical facts against the source system before acting.
Log and diff all proposed file or container changes.
requires-engineering: implement a verification layer between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context, while slim handles certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if the same regulated data class flows through both, especially because slim’s network egress is broad and its secrets handling is explicit. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in MemMachine and then processed by slim, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF registry credentials or private keys are present in slim’s workspace, compliance obligations increase.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of slim’s workspace.
Document which data classes may flow between the agents.
Set short retention windows for any shared artifacts.
Review whether any data crosses residency boundaries before execution.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both systems.
